questions.question: You open a terminal in your project folder and want Claude's help with the code there. What do you type?
questions.explanation: Running claude in a folder starts a session scoped to that project. /help only works once a session is running, and there is no /start command.

questions.question: In a session, you want to check your Python version yourself and let Claude see the result. What do you type?
questions.explanation: One ! runs the rest of the line in the shell, and the output lands in the conversation. A / starts a Claude Code command, and a second ! gets passed to the shell.

questions.question: You typed ! and then pasted a line that starts with its own !. The shell replies "command not found". Why?
options: The shell received a command starting with !
Shell commands are blocked in this mode
questions.answer: The shell received a command starting with !
questions.explanation: Claude Code removes only the first !, so the shell received !python --version, which isn't a command.

questions.question: You've finished one task and want to start an unrelated one without the old conversation getting in the way. Which command do you run?
questions.explanation: /clear starts a fresh conversation. /config opens settings, and /help lists commands.

questions.question: You want Claude to add a login page to your app, and you want to check its approach before any files change. What should you do?
options: Switch to plan mode and review the plan
Let Claude build it, then review the diff
questions.answer: Switch to plan mode and review the plan
questions.explanation: In plan mode Claude only reads and researches, then waits for you to approve its plan before editing anything. Reviewing the diff afterwards means the files have already changed.
